correctness.rationale: The source norm formula reduces exactly to minimizing \(a+b\) over affine majorants of the continuous nonnegative profile \(m_f\). Since \(a+b=2L(1/2)\), the infimum is twice the least concave majorant at one-half. The concavification formula at a single barycenter is a linear program over probability measures with two moment constraints, whose extreme measures have support at at most two points, yielding the displayed two-slice maximum. Compactness gives attainment and the diagonal case is the continuous limit.

final_claim: For \(C(K_1)*C(K_2)\), if \(m_f(t)=\max_{x,y}|f([x,y,t])|\), then the free-product norm equals \(2\,\operatorname{conc}(m_f)(1/2)\), equivalently an attained maximum over at most two join-parameter slices with barycenter one-half.
limitations: The formula is correct and potentially useful computationally.
